title: Cross-SDK resilience defaults, idempotency tooling, and failure taxonomy
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Design and land a cross-language (Python/TypeScript/Go) set of defaults and ergonomics for client-side retries, backoff shapes, idempotency tooling, and a canonical taxonomy of retryable vs non-retryable failures. This ticket collects the final decisions, the code examples for each SDK, QA checklist, and rollout plan for a conservative safe default that keeps higher-level product SLAs intact while minimizing surprising duplicate work for customers.
acceptance_criteria: A single documented default retry policy exists for all SDKs (stable configuration values and rationale).
A small, supported idempotency header + helper exists in each SDK to allow customers to opt-in to deduplication for non-idempotent endpoints.
A published failure taxonomy (retryable/transient vs non-retryable vs conditional) is in docs and used by SDKs for default behavior.
Streaming ergonomics guidance published: resumable streams where feasible, automatic short-circuit on known non-retryable streaming errors, and example code in Python/TS/Go.
Integration tests covering retries, idempotency header propagation, and streaming resume behavior in CI for the three SDKs.
Rollout feature flag enabling gradual enforcement/telemetry of SDK retry defaults.
Implementation PRs created for each SDK and basic docs/CHANGELOG entries.
Stakeholder sign-off from API, Console, and Runtime teams recorded in comments.
design_decisions: Use a conservative default 3-attempt policy: attempts = 3, initial_backoff_ms = 100, multiplier = 2.0, max_backoff_ms = 2000, jitter_frac = 0.25. Rationale: balances transient infrastructure glitches without adding large tail latency for typical request patterns.

Classify errors into three categories: RETRYABLE_TRANSIENT (5xx, throttling 429 with retry-after absent), CONDITIONAL_RETRYABLE (429 with Retry-After, or server 'retryable' flag), and NON_RETRYABLE (4xx client errors, validation failures).

Expose idempotency via header 'X-Redwood-Idempotency' and optional 'X-Redwood-Idempotency-Expiry' (seconds). SDKs provide helper to generate UUIDv4 ids and attach these headers for user-controlled operations (create, mutate endpoints).

Default SDK behavior: do not auto-generate idempotency headers for opaque user content; we provide a small helper so customers can opt-in. Auto-generation only for convenience in high-level convenience methods where semantics are clearly documented.

Streaming retry approach: prefer resumable streams with server-provided resume token. If resume not supported, fall back to client-side checkpointing based on last-ack'd message and re-invocation with explicit offsets where feasible.

Telemetry: SDKs should emit a small set of events to telemetry (retry_attempt, final_result, idempotency_key_present, resume_token_used) behind an opt-out flag to monitor real-world behavior during rollout.

Language ergonomics: API surface should be idiomatic per-language (sync/async for Python, callback/async iterator for TS, context-managed for Go). But core config names remain consistent: maxAttempts, initialBackoffMs, multiplier, maxBackoffMs, jitterFraction, idempotencyHeader.
implementation_notes: Add a new shared design doc and canonical constants file in SDK repo roots (SDKs share markdown and examples).
Provide a single configuration schema used by all SDKs; language bindings translate types but preserve field names and units (ms for time windows).

SDK helper: Idempotency.generate() -> UUID, Idempotency.attach(headers, expirySeconds?) -> mutated headers, and Idempotency.validateOnServerResponse(response) to allow clients to detect deduplication outcomes.

Edge-case: For streaming 'append' style APIs, idempotency must be viewable as 'idempotent append' by server; document required server-side guarantee; otherwise, mark streaming append as non-idempotent by default.
Backoff randomness: implement full jitter (random between 0 and current_backoff) to avoid synchronized retries across clients.
Expose easy opt-in flags: allow_disable_retries, allow_disable_idempotency_auto, telemetry_enabled default true for rollout window.
examples:
Python - simple retry and idempotency helper:

from redwood import RedwoodClient, Idempotency

client = RedwoodClient(retry_config={
    'maxAttempts': 3,
    'initialBackoffMs': 100,
    'multiplier': 2.0,
    'maxBackoffMs': 2000,
    'jitterFraction': 0.25,
})

headers = {}
key = Idempotency.generate()  # UUIDv4
Idempotency.attach(headers, key, expiry_seconds=60)
res = client.create_document(text='hello world', headers=headers)
print(res)

Streaming resume fallback pseudocode (server lacks resume token):

1) client persists last-processed message index N locally every M messages.
2) on transient network failure, client reconnects and issues an idempotent 'replay from N+1' request using idempotency header.
3) server must support request param 'start_offset' for this to be safe; if not, document non-resumable stream semantics.
testing_plan: Unit tests per SDK for backoff math and jitter distribution (deterministic jitter using seeded PRNG for unit tests).
Integration tests in CI: inject synthetic 500/429 errors with and without Retry-After to verify behavior and metrics.
End-to-end streaming tests: simulate mid-stream network cut and verify resume token persists and resume returns consistent delivery (idempotency used to avoid duplicates).
Performance test: ensure default retry config does not materially increase P50/P95 latency in stable environment (compare with opt-out flag).
Telemetry validation: tests to assert SDK emits the expected telemetry events when telemetry_enabled=true.
Security: verify idempotency headers are not logged by default in debug logs; redact in SDK logging helpers.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): merge SDK changes behind feature flag; release to canary channel and enable for 5% of new SDK installs. Collect telemetry for 2 weeks.
Phase 1 (observe): increase to 25% for 1 week; run integration test matrix against runtime and console to verify no regressions in usage patterns.
Phase 2 (gradual enable): 50% for 1 week; reach out to top customers with opt-out instructions in case of incompatibilities.
Phase 3 (full): flip default on for new SDK versions in package registries and document in CHANGELOG with migration guide. Existing pinned versions unchanged unless a customer opts-in.
risks: Auto-generating idempotency keys for the wrong operation may give customers a false sense of deduplication — mitigated by requiring explicit helper usage or clear opt-in at high-level convenience APIs.
Synchronized retries across many clients without adequate jitter could spike load on runtime. Full jitter policy recommended.
Streams without resume support may produce partial duplicates or lost progress; require clear documentation and prefer server resume token API for safe resume semantics.
Telemetry privacy concerns: ensure no sensitive request payloads are attached to retry telemetry events.
